title: Cut a DIN rail to length on a powered rail cutter
instruction: Cut a 250 mm length off the right end of the rail with the rail cutter.
context: Electricians and panel assemblers cut DIN rail to length for every control panel they build: set the rail at the mark on the cutter's scale, clamp it, press the cut button. A rail cut short is scrap.
setup: A powered bench DIN-rail cutter fixed to the table, rail path 0.32 m in front of the arm bases, left to right, blade 0.04 m right of their midline. Blue steel body: infeed ledge (60 mm wide, 40 mm tall) from 12 to 680 mm left of the blade with two guide fences (3 x 4 mm, inner faces 14 mm either side of the rail path); a die 24 mm long, opening 37 x 9.5 mm; a cutting head over it (64 x 44 x 110 mm, guarded blade, rated 30 kN, stroke 1 s down); outfeed ledge (60 x 40 mm) from 12 to 330 mm right, with a length scale on its top measured from the blade (marks every 10 mm to 300 mm), no length stop. A toggle clamp 45 mm left of the blade: 205 mm arm hinged behind the rail, red handle toward the arms, rubber pad over the rail, open at 45 degrees, snaps shut past 20 degrees. A console 65-105 mm in front of the rail path, 35-75 mm right of the blade, 60 mm tall, red 20 mm cut button (3 mm press starts a stroke, only with the clamp shut). A loose steel TS35 x 7.5 rail, 600 mm, 0.2 kg, open side up, on the infeed ledge between the fences, its right end 40 mm short of the blade.
scoring: The cut is the blade's first stroke (it runs only with the clamp shut), made at the bottom of the stroke; only it counts. 1.0: the rail in the die, its right end 250 mm past the blade within 1 mm, and it moved under 0.5 mm along the cutter during the stroke. 0.5: otherwise, cut in the die within 5 mm of 250 mm. 0.25: otherwise, no such cut, but before the cut the rail lay in the die with its end within 5 mm of 250 mm for 1 s without a break. 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: Each real trial uses a new 600 mm rail (the cut consumes it); measure the cut piece with a ruler. Open the clamp. In the simulation nothing is cut, so the rail is reset to its start.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz. The blade is a look only and the rail is not divided: the cut is the stroke reaching the bottom, the cut length the rail's position then. The cutter's motor and the cutting force are not simulated: the blade follows its stroke. Generic cutter design.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; its arms moved over the cutter's ends but never gripped the rail, clamp or button); scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 729: rail set, clamp shut, button pressed, cut 249.5 mm, rail still). README checks: 3 mm short 0.5; clamp open, no cut 0.25.
